text:
Frank Nazar has put Chicago's slide on himself. The Daily Herald asked how the Blackhawks stop the bleeding, and Nazar said it starts with him. He scored twice in Wednesday's loss, one of them a shorthanded breakaway that The Athletic's Mark Lazerus called "A beauty," but the Hawks are still winless on the road (Chicago Tribune), and Nazar has seven points in 15 games.

The numbers are on his side more than the scoreboard suggests. His own chances are up to just over a goal of expected value per 60 minutes, among the better rates for a young forward, and he is one of the fastest skaters in the league with a top-ten-percent shot. Chicago is losing the 5v5 chance battle with him on (46%), but much less badly than without him, and his teammates have scored 8.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve while he is out there. That is the biggest single reason his point total looks thin, and it tends to swing back. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with some of the weakest teammates in the league. Our projection: about 21 goals and 44 points.
headline: Nazar is carrying more than his share
